question: Should OpenClaw adopt agent-controlled continuation, delegated future work, and voluntary compaction as a supported core runtime contract, and if so which minimal configuration and session-routing guarantees should be public?
rationale: The PR adds a new durable scheduling and session-enrichment capability rather than repairing an established contract; choosing its long-term core scope, cross-session policy, and operator surface requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core design
options.body: Keep the capability in core, but split the continuation implementation into reviewable slices with an explicit public config, persistence, and cross-session contract.

options.title: Keep existing scheduling model
options.body: Decline the new continuation contract and retain existing event, heartbeat, cron, and subagent mechanisms as the supported paths.

options.title: Prototype outside core first
options.body: Ask for a plugin or experimental implementation until a smaller core extension seam is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed core design
recommendation.body: Keep the capability in core, but split the continuation implementation into reviewable slices with an explicit public config, persistence, and cross-session contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied timeline is the only maintainer-facing routing signal for this broad product decision.
